threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Rust DOCX comparison/edit/inspection/rendering engine exposed through native CLI, PyO3 Python facade/CLI, WASM byte APIs/Node CLI, and an optional Python stdio MCP server (src/lib.rs:5-35; jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:42-49; jubarte-wasm/cli/package.json:33-46).
assets: Document contents, revisions, comments, metadata, generated DOCX/PDF/PNG, edit snapshots and reports; host input/output files and engine process availability.

Installed executable and release integrity; updater selects jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines assets and SHA256SUMS.txt, with currently empty RELEASE_KEYS and no FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted package bytes enter bounded admission before document operations; default input budgets are 64 MiB compressed/per part, 256 MiB inflated, 10000 entries and XML depth 256; compare budgets instead allow 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflated (src/admission.rs:63-100).

MCP stdio clients obtain document I/O under operator-selected --root (default cwd); _OutputRoot holds a cap-std directory handle for relative reads/publication; read/write ToolAnnotations are hints, while capability-relative I/O enforces containment (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199).
Native CLI publish_paths has ambient filesystem authority, held parent handles and staged per-file commits; OutputRoot is a separately confined interface (src/publication.rs:203-225,421-569).
attackerCapabilities: A sender can provide malicious DOCX/DOC/XML/font/image bytes and edit or Markdown content to a willing caller; no remote listener or tenant identity is inferred.

An MCP client can request supported tools and overwrite=true inside the granted root; it does not thereby possess operator environment, release signing keys, or repository publish authority (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152-160,258-277,373-381).
securityObjectives: Preserve bounded parsing, package identity, safe path handling, and checked XML policy before materializing untrusted input; callers own OS memory/CPU confinement (SECURITY.md:35-79).

Confine MCP document reads and outputs to held root authority; never confuse read-only tool hints with enforcement (src/publication.rs:146-199; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108).
assumptions: No deployment context or authoritative threat model supplied; userContext is null. Analysis is offline and current-state-only.

Native rendering additionally reads installed fonts and persists font-index.tsv beside the user font folder, with JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overriding or disabling; MCP --root does not encompass those independent native renderer operations (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3095-3107,3213-3229).

Byte-in/byte-out library docs say no temp files (src/lib.rs:8-11), but native font indexing writes a sibling tsv.<pid>.tmp then renames; retain this qualification, not a vulnerability claim (src/convert/font.rs:3213-3229).

findings.title: Rendering an HTML altChunk can exhaust memory through its colspan
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a related HTML table containing `colspan=1000000000` makes the converter append one billion XML grid columns. The input stays tiny and passes archive admission, but PDF, PNG, and layout-report operations can consume excessive CPU and memory or terminate their host process.

severity.rationale: A document sender can drive enormous allocation during ordinary rendering without control of local files or configuration. The established consequence is process availability loss; no remote service or broader compromise is assumed. Caller-enforced process CPU/memory limits contain impact.
severity.changeConditions: A deployed shared rendering service would increase operational impact; enforcing a cumulative expansion budget before the loop would remove the path.

confidence.rationale: Direct source traces public rendering through admitted package bytes to HTML parsing, unchecked numeric span and its allocation loop; no runtime trigger was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Render imports a related HTML chunk after admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Untrusted DOCX bytes are admitted, then the related chunk bytes are passed to `altchunk::expand` before DOM construction.

codeEvidence.label: Resolve and translate HTML bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: The document relationship ID selects package bytes; `chunk_html` decodes them and calls `html_to_wml`.

codeEvidence.label: Accept unbounded HTML colspan
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-controlled `colspan` is parsed as `usize` with only a lower bound, then stored in the cell span stack.

codeEvidence.label: Emit one XML column per numeric span
codeEvidence.explanation: `end_table` sums the stored spans and emits `cols` grid records into an expanding String without a column or output-byte budget.

codeEvidence.label: Dispatch each parsed HTML tag
codeEvidence.explanation: The HTML tokenizer forwards opening cell and closing table tags to the builder, preserving numeric attribute input.

codeEvidence.label: Close tables through end_table
codeEvidence.explanation: A closing table tag triggers the expansion loop in `end_table`.

rootCause.summary: Package admission bounds archive bytes, inflated parts, and XML syntax, but HTML-to-WML expansion occurs afterwards. `Builder::start` accepts arbitrarily large representable `colspan`, stores it in `cell_spans`, and `end_table` uses the row span sum as the exact count of XML grid records to generate. The expanded output has no resource budget.

findings.remediation: Apply a small maximum HTML colspan and cumulative table-column budget before storing spans, use checked arithmetic for row sums, and enforce a cumulative generated-WML byte budget with a typed refusal before allocating.

counterEvidence: Archive admission runs before expansion and limits actual input bytes, not the numeric span or generated XML (src/admission.rs:531-551).
Existing tests handle invalid, negative and zero spans and ordinary span 2, but show no maximum-span rejection (src/convert/altchunk.rs:1026-1054).
SECURITY.md requires hosts to apply process CPU/memory limits; these mitigate host scope but do not bound this loop.
limitations: No application execution or vulnerability-triggering input was used in this static audit.
validation.summary: `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

controls: Archive byte/XML limits apply before expansion.
Host process limits can contain a worker failure.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> `with_layout` -> package relationship -> `expand` -> `html_to_wml` -> numeric `cell_spans` -> `end_table` XML expansion
dataflow.outcome: Excessive CPU/memory consumption and possible process termination

impact.why: Rendering process availability and memory budget are affected.

likelihood.why: A short representable numeric attribute directly controls the expansion count.

reachability.summary: Any caller exposing supported PDF/PNG/layout APIs to documents from another party can trigger this path; no service deployment, special flag, local file write, or raised input limits is required.
preconditions: Victim renders a supplied DOCX with an internal HTML altChunk relationship.

attackPath.summary: Provide a valid DOCX with `w:altChunk` referencing a short HTML table whose single cell has a very large positive `colspan`, then have a caller render it.

remediationTests: Reject huge representable positive colspan through public rendering while retaining ordinary span behavior.
Verify many bounded spans cannot exceed the cumulative table/output budget.
Verify row-span sum overflow returns a refusal on native and wasm32.
preventiveControls: Budget derived representations before materialization, including post-admission HTML/MHT expansion.

findings.title: Rendering a tiny table can allocate billions of columns
findings.summary: A DOCX containing a cell with `w:gridSpan=2147483647`, or an equivalent `w:gridBefore`/`w:gridAfter`, drives the renderer to allocate approximately 8 GiB for a column-width vector. Archive admission accepts these short numeric attributes, so PDF, PNG and layout operations can exhaust memory or terminate their embedding process.

severity.rationale: A document provider controls the count that reaches allocation during ordinary rendering. Process availability is the demonstrated impact and likelihood is high; no remotely exposed service is assumed. Caller process limits restrict blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Shared-service deployment would increase impact; a semantic table-column budget checked before arithmetic/allocation would remove the path.

confidence.rationale: Source directly connects the three numeric span fields through RawCell occupancy to vec allocation; no runtime reproduction was performed.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span` and `row_grid_skip` accept numeric column counts without a semantic maximum. Table parsing retains them as RawCell spans, including before/after placeholder cells. `stretch_stale_spans` leaves an oversized row unchanged, and its span sum then controls column-vector allocation. Package input bounds do not bound this derived representation.

findings.remediation: Reject individual spans and cumulative table occupancy above a documented column budget before arithmetic or allocation. Use checked addition and return a typed conversion refusal for invalid numeric semantics.

counterEvidence: Byte/XML admission does not validate numeric table semantics.
Markdown's separate table reader clamps spans to 64 (src/markdown/from_docx/mod.rs:3590-3595), but rendering does not call that reader.
SECURITY.md directs callers to process memory/CPU limits.
limitations: Static-only validation; memory exhaustion was not triggered.
validation.summary: The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell.

findings.title: Rendering extreme list levels performs billions of operations
findings.summary: A DOCX paragraph with `w:ilvl=4294967295` and an ordinary numbering definition forces a reverse scan over billions of undefined levels. Defining a very high abstract level or override additionally makes the renderer initialize a counter for every lower level, exhausting CPU and memory.

severity.rationale: A document sender can force extreme work with a tiny numeric field during normal layout. The established impact is worker/process availability loss; no remote deployment is inferred. Host process limits can contain the failure.
severity.changeConditions: Exposure as a shared document service increases operational impact; bounded supported levels and key-based parent lookup remove the path.

confidence.rationale: Source establishes unrestricted paragraph, abstract and override levels and all numeric-range loops; no timing or allocation trigger was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Render imports a related HTML chunk after admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Untrusted DOCX bytes are admitted, then the related chunk bytes are passed to `altchunk::expand` before DOM construction.

codeEvidence.label: Paragraph list level is unbounded
codeEvidence.explanation: Direct and style paragraph numbering reads `ilvl` as arbitrary u32 and retains it.

codeEvidence.label: Resolve parent by scanning numeric range
codeEvidence.explanation: An undefined high level makes `resolve_ilvl` inspect every lower integer until a defined parent is found.

codeEvidence.label: Synthesize level through another numeric scan
codeEvidence.explanation: `ensure_level` repeats a reverse parent search over the unbounded level range when a direct level is absent.

codeEvidence.label: Marker dispatch preserves resolved level
codeEvidence.explanation: `next_marker` passes the arbitrary resolved level to subsequent counter initialization.

codeEvidence.label: Initialize a counter for every lower number
codeEvidence.explanation: An explicitly defined high level makes this loop grow the counters map for all lower integers.

codeEvidence.label: Render scans levels again
codeEvidence.explanation: Marker rendering also enumerates all levels up to an unbounded ilvl.

codeEvidence.label: Abstract numbering levels accept high indices
codeEvidence.explanation: Parsed abstract `ilvl` keys enter the numbering map without a supported-range check.

codeEvidence.label: Overrides accept high indices
codeEvidence.explanation: Full level overrides independently preserve arbitrary level indices in the effective level map.

rootCause.summary: `num_pr` retains arbitrary u32 paragraph levels, and abstract/override parsers accept the same unsupported index range. `resolve_ilvl` and `ensure_level` search integer ranges rather than defined levels. For a high defined level, `next_marker` creates every missing lower counter, and marker rendering enumerates the range again.

findings.remediation: Enforce the supported numbering level range at paragraph, style, abstract and override boundaries, normally 0 through 8. Resolve parents by examining defined keys, and bound all counter initialization and rendering loops.

counterEvidence: XML depth bounds are independent of numeric level values.
Markdown separately clamps ilvl to 8 (src/markdown/from_docx/mod.rs:2655-2664); renderer uses its own Numbering implementation.
Host CPU/memory limits can terminate or constrain a worker.
limitations: Static validation only; billions of operations were not executed.
validation.summary: Paragraph numbering and style inheritance use num_pr without an ilvl cap (src/convert/mod.rs:12683-12718,12834-12879). An undefined u32-max paragraph level reaches resolve_ilvl's reverse scan with an ordinary level-zero parent. A defined high level bypasses that search but reaches the counters loop. Abstract levels and full overrides have no upper-bound check, so both paths remain reachable after admission.

dataflow.summary: Paragraph/style numPr or abstract/override XML -> arbitrary ilvl -> Numbering resolution -> numeric-range hash lookups / counter insertion / marker rendering

likelihood.why: Short numeric input directly drives large ranges.

reachability.summary: Supported render/layout APIs process document-supplied numbering without any feature flag or raised admission limit.
reachability.outcome: CPU saturation and possibly large counter-map allocation

attackPath.summary: Provide a DOCX list paragraph requesting a very high numeric level and have a caller render or lay it out.

remediationTests: Reject or safely normalize u32-max paragraph, abstract and override levels.
Verify sparse definitions do not trigger iteration proportional to an undefined numeric index.
preventiveControls: Use a validated bounded numbering-level type throughout the renderer.
